**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
[Sometimes you have a recipe with ridiculous amounts of time going into it, e.g. a Baguette recipe with 72h proofing time.] For bread baking e.g. on Saturday preparation steps may have to be performed on Thursday and Friday, adding the days would add clarity.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
In addition to adjusting the time display format it would be helpful to also display the day of the week for each of the involved steps. Example: 17:45 Thursday instead of just 17:45. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Ideally days are displayed as soon as beginning of step 1 and ending of the last step are not on the same day.
- Instead of showing the weekday one could add e.g. "+1d" with an enumeration for every 24h that have lapsed since the start time of the recipe. Example: if 17:45 is the start time, next morning 6:45 would show as 6:45 but that day 18:00 would show as "18:00 (+1d)" This would work without localization and possibly be simple solution. This would make the recipe independet from the calendar.

Opened #4785 for this.

Recipe and step times render as `1 h 30 min` above the hour and `72 h` for a long proof
instead of `4320 min` — at both recipe detail layouts, the recipe card chip (which
previously showed a bare number with no unit at all) and the step timer button. No day
rollover, matching the table earlier in this thread. It sits behind a per-user preference
that defaults off, so nothing changes for existing users unless they turn it on.

One thing worth noting for anyone arriving here from a search: #3751 and #3778 are linked
above and look like they closed this, but what they add is the localized `+2 Days` suffix on
the running step timer's "Finished at" line. That is a different surface, and it works — the
recipe page itself still shows raw minutes today.

Happy to reshape the PR: the test tooling is a separate commit that can be dropped, and the
default is a one-line change if on-by-default would be preferred.

The other half of my original ask here — the weekday on each step — is not in #4785 by design, since it needs an anchor to a wall clock that the recipe page doesn't have today. I've proposed it separately on #1882 (Time Rework), where it fits the "multi day recipes" item: https://github.com/TandoorRecipes/recipes/issues/1882#issuecomment-5276392328

Briefly: you give the recipe a finish time and it back-chains a start time per step, so a bake due Sunday morning tells you when to mix the levain on Thursday. It ended up using both alternatives I floated in 2022 — weekday names near in, and the explicit `(−9 d)` offset once the span passes a week and a bare weekday stops being unambiguous. Frontend only, and it picks the finish time up from the meal planner automatically.
